To interpret spatial directions consistently across different viewing angles, To interpret spatial directions consistently across different viewing angles, we define a right-handed orthogonal coordinate system as follows:

1. z-axis (vertical): Let g denote the gravity vector (pointing downward). Define \hat{z} = -g/||g|| so that +z points upward (opposite to gravity) and -z points downward.

2. y-axis (forward/backward): Let c denote the camera optical axis. Project c onto the plane orthogonal to \hat{z}: c_perp = c - (c · \hat{z}) \hat{z}. Normalize to obtain \hat{y} = c_perp / ||c_perp||, choosing the orientation such that the angle between \hat{y} and c is acute (< 90°). Then +y corresponds to forward, -y to backward.

3. x-axis (right/left): Define \hat{x} = \hat{y} × \hat{z}. This completes a right-handed system, where +x points right and -x points left.

Directional convention: +z = upward, -z = downward; +y = forward, -y = backward; +x = right, -x = left.
